/itinerary_variants/1/stops/2/highlights.source_en: **0.8 km boardwalk loop**, ~15 min walk — barrier-free deck, wheelchair/stroller accessible
Part of **Jeju Global Geopark (UNESCO 2010-10)** — 13 island-wide geosites
Admission **₩2,000 adult / ₩1,000 youth / FREE under 7 + over 65**
Hallasan summit visible to the north on clear days, **directly downstream** geologically

/itinerary_variants/1/stops/2/whyOnRoute.source_en: **⟦G0⟧ is a compact, high-impact geology stop.** The viewing deck gives guests a clear look at Jeju's columnar basalt cliffs without a long hike, and the site fits naturally after Hallasan 1100 Highland before the route continues toward Seogwipo. The guide may adjust photo time depending on wind, tide, and crowd levels.

/itinerary_variants/1/stops/2/descriptio.source_en: **⟦G0⟧ (대포 주상절리)** is one of Jeju's clearest examples of columnar basalt along the coast. Lava from Hallasan-area volcanic activity cooled and contracted into tightly packed polygonal stone columns, creating the dramatic cliff line now viewed from a safe seaside deck. The columns rise above the waves on the Jungmun coast and are especially photogenic when the sea is active. The visit is short, high-impact, and easier than a long coastal hike, making it a strong stop for mixed-age groups. Walking is mostly on maintained paths and viewing platforms, but wind and sea spray can vary by weather and tide.

/itinerary_variants/1/stops/3/highlights.source_en: **Galchi sashimi**, **black pork BBQ**, or vegetarian Bibimbap + Mom-guk options
~60 min duration — fits cruise day-trip timeline
**5-min walk to ⟦G0⟧ trailhead** — most efficient lunch-to-attraction flow

/itinerary_variants/1/stops/3/whyOnRoute.source_en: **Lunch near Seogwipo Maeil Olle Market keeps the south route efficient.** The area has many local restaurants and sits close to ⟦G0⟧, so the group can eat, walk, and continue the afternoon route without a long transfer. It also gives guests an easy introduction to local foods before the short return toward Gangjeong Port later in the day.

/itinerary_variants/1/stops/3/descriptio.source_en: **Seogwipo lunch stop** at a guide-vetted local restaurant near Seogwipo Maeil Olle Market or the ⟦G0⟧ area. Typical choices may include hairtail, black pork, abalone porridge, seafood dishes, or simple vegetarian-friendly meals depending on the restaurant and group preference. Lunch is normally paid separately unless an included-lunch option has been arranged in advance. After lunch, the route continues efficiently toward ⟦G0⟧ and the market area without unnecessary backtracking.

/itinerary_variants/1/stops/4/highlights.source_en: **Single-tier cascade 22 m × 12 m into 20 m-deep emerald pool** — Seogwipo's signature waterfall
**NOT Cheonjeyeon (천제연)** — different falls, different gorge, ~15 min west in Jungmun
**Mutae eel (Natural Monument No. 27)** habitat — nocturnal marbled eel under illumination
**Damselfly Tree (Natural Monument No. 163)** + Crepidomanes makinoi ferns line the gorge
Gentle **1 km paved trail (~15 min)** — stroller/wheelchair friendly
**19:00–22:00 night illumination** — unique among Jeju waterfalls
**5-min walk from ⟦G0⟧** — natural pairing for south-route cruise days

/itinerary_variants/1/stops/4/whyOnRoute.source_en: **⟦G1⟧ adds an easy nature walk near Seogwipo.** The riverside path is gentler than many of Jeju's steeper coastal or mountain stops, so it works well after lunch. The waterfall, forested gorge, and pool give the south route a softer landscape contrast after Hallasan and Jusangjeolli. The guide also helps guests distinguish ⟦G1⟧ in Seogwipo from ⟦G0⟧ in Jungmun, which has a similar English spelling but is a different site.

/itinerary_variants/1/stops/4/descriptio.source_en: **⟦G1⟧** (천지연 폭포 — literally 'Sky-meeting-Land Falls') is the closer-to-port of Seogwipo's two famous waterfalls and is **NOT to be confused with ⟦G0⟧** (천제연 — the three-tier 'Pond of the Heavenly Emperor' falls in Jungmun, ~15 min west). The single-tier cascade plunges **22 m / 12 m wide into a 20 m-deep emerald pool** at the end of a **gentle 1 km riverside trail** (~15 min one-way, paved and stroller-friendly) that follows a subtropical gorge dense with **rare plants**: **Damselfly Tree** (Natural Monument No. 163), **Crepidomanes makinoi** ferns clinging to the basalt walls, and dozens of endemic species protected as **Natural Monument No. 379** (the falls + surrounding habitat ensemble). The pool below is the protected habitat of the **Mutae eel** (마부태 / 무태 — *Anguilla marmorata*, the marbled eel), itself **Natural Monument No. 27** — a nocturnal species whose movement under nighttime illumination is one of Cheonjiyeon's signature scenes. Admission is **₩2,000 adults / ₩1,000 children** (one of Jeju's most affordable nature stops); operating hours **09:00–22:00 (last entry 21:30)** — the **after-dark illumination program 19:00–22:00** is unique among Jeju waterfalls and turns the gorge walls + falls into an emerald-jade light show, often paired with cruise overnight stays. The trailhead is **a 5-minute walk from ⟦G2⟧**, making the two stops a natural pairing on cruise day-trips originating from Gangjeong port. On clear days, **Munseom Island** (3 km offshore — Korea's first marine-park designation, 1994) is visible from the falls observation deck, and the basalt cliff faces of the gorge expose the same Hallasan-flank lava-flow stratigraphy as Daepo Jusangjeolli.

/itinerary_variants/1/stops/5/highlights.source_en: **South Jeju's largest traditional market** — 620 m arcade, ~200 shops, ~140 vendors
**Olle Trail Courses 6 & 7** pass near the market entrance
**Jeseong Bakery octopus buns** — local cult favorite, queues by 10:00
